exposure: maternal exposure to drinking water nitrosamines
cohort: The study included 2457 mother-infant pairs from a single drinking water supply system in central China.
finding: Elevated maternal N-nitrosodimethylamine (NDMA) exposure in the second trimester and N-nitrosopiperidine (NPIP) exposure during the entire pregnancy were associated with decreased birth weight and increased risks of preterm delivery, while elevated N-nitrosodiethylamine (NDEA) exposure in the second trimester was associated with increased risk of small for gestational age.
